messages:
sandhya: Heads-up — received a model tarball from an external researcher (Harbor-13B). They included a CONTRIBUTING.md and a short license note. Need quick legal/export check before we add to model-catalog.

jordan (Legal): Can you paste the license excerpt here? Also who is the contributor (company/individual) and country? export control stuff depends on origin and tech specs.

sandhya: Contributor: individual in Singapore. License text: 
```
"By contributing, you grant Redwood a perpetual, non-exclusive, worldwide license to host, modify, and provide commercial services using the model. Contributor retains IP. No warranty. Export-control: contributor asserts no restrictions."
```

matt: Quick context: this model is a standard transformer, 13B, no dual-use claim in readme. Our evals show hallucination risk on medical prompts but nothing red-flaggy for weapons.

jordan (Legal): Two immediate flags: 1) "perpetual commercial license" sounds fine but we need explicit indemnity/warranties clause for third-party data. 2) "contributor asserts no restrictions" is ambiguous — we need an express export control statement and provenance (training data sources).

liz: From infra: if legal needs provenance we'll probably block adding to hosted catalog until cleared. We can stage it on Dedicated sandbox for internal experiments. :eyes:

sandhya: Noted. Contributor also added a model card snippet: 
```
training_data: mixture of web crawl + public books.
filtered_pii: yes (regex + heuristics)
fine_tuning: none
```

jordan (Legal): Still insufficient. Ask for: 1) signed contributor agreement (CLA) with explicit grant to host/commercialize and warranty re: third-party data; 2) export-control self-cert stating country of origin of training compute + any restricted data; 3) list of pretraining corpora or proportional sources (or reasonable summary).

matt: For immediate experiments, can we run quantization/benchmarks on a private Dedicated queue while legal sorts CLA? I want to test 8-bit/4-bit perf/quality tradeoffs.

jordan (Legal): That's acceptable if it's locked to an internal sandbox and we don't expose inference externally. Also ensure logs and checksum artifacts are stored in customer-isolated bucket.

sandhya: I'll message contributor with a short checklist and request PDF-signed CLA + dataset provenance + export stmt. Draft reply below — pls quick review: 
"Thanks — before we onboard Harbor-13B to Redwood's catalog we need (1) a signed Contributor License Agreement granting Redwood hosting and commercial rights and basic warranties, (2) a short provenance statement listing major data sources and confirmation no restricted datasets were used, (3) an export-control attestation including contributor country and compute origin. We can run private infra experiments while this is pending. Please sign the CLA at <link>." 

jordan (Legal): Good. Add a line about model weights: whether weights include any third-party embeddings or proprietary layers. Also request contact for takedown/incident response.

sandhya: Updated message sent. Contributor replied: "Can sign CLA, training data mostly public web corpora + CC-licensed books, compute in Singapore, no third-party proprietary embeddings." They attached a signed PDF (placeholder).

ops-oncall: deploy-bot reports: "model-staging job queued for harbors/harbor-13b quant-8bit on dedicated-sandbox-2, id: job_8812"

matt: I'll kick off a quick quantization sweep (8-bit, 4-bit) and a small eval suite (MMLU subset, safety prompt set). Will share metrics.

jordan (Legal): Once you have evaluation artifacts, include: sample prompts that hit failure modes, perplexity on held-out, and any hallucination examples. We'll attach them to CLA file in case of future disputes.

sandhya: Thanks all. Plan: 1) legal confirms CLA validity (Jordan) 2) matt runs quant/evals in sandbox (Matt) 3) infra keeps it isolated (Liz/ops) 4) if all clear, schedule model-catalog intake review next Tue.

matt: Starting runs now. ETA ~4h. :rocket:
